note: Chapter XVII full pass in the Book I painting style (Ian, 17 Nov), shot-sized.
style: A cinematic Romantic oil painting of 1893 in the exact manner of the reference painting: academic realism with dramatic chiaroscuro, warm amber lamplight and firelight against deep brown-black shadow, a cool blue window, atmospheric haze and shafts of light, deep architectural space, rich painterly brushwork. One single painting filling the whole 16:9 frame, no text, signature, border or black bars.

beats.text: Shot: medium. In the dim marble hall of a London hotel, the elderly clean-shaven professor reads a telegram while the young doctor waits beside him; grey window light, a porter in the background.
Shot: medium. In a hotel sitting-room, the elderly clean-shaven professor hands a bundle of papers to the young doctor, speaking earnestly; window light, travelling bag on a chair.
Shot: medium. On the steam-filled platform, the young doctor greets the sweet-faced young woman, who holds out her gloved hand; porters and travellers around them in shafts of light.

Shot: wide. Inside a gas-lit carriage of the London Underground in 1893: the doctor and the young woman sit opposite each other on wooden benches, a typewriter case at her feet, the dark tunnel beyond the glass.
Shot: wide. The cold stone entrance hall of the asylum: the young woman shudders as she steps in beside the doctor; an attendant at a far door, a single lamp, long shadows.

Shot: medium. From the dark hall, looking past the young woman who has paused to listen at a half-open study door; through the gap, the doctor sits alone in lamplight speaking into the tube of a phonograph.

Shot: wide, far. A big book-lined study seen from the far corner: the young woman in the doorway, surprised, the doctor rising from beside a phonograph on the desk; blue window light and one warm lamp.
Shot: close. Close on the young doctor's face, horror-struck, one hand raised as if to ward off a question; lamplight from one side.
Shot: medium. The young woman, seated by the phonograph, quietly offers to copy the diary on her typewriter; the doctor, pale, turns away toward the window.
Shot: close detail. The doctor's hands opening a large drawer packed with rows of black wax phonograph cylinders, lamplight glinting on them.
Shot: wide, far, high angle. Looking down a dark panelled stair hall: the doctor carries the heavy phonograph up the stairs, the young woman ahead with a candle, their shadows climbing the walls.
